feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform roles: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by useful scale indicators. It reads clearly overall, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce polish.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression within NACo from coordinator to director to consultant, which reinforces credibility and growth.  
- Good impact signals: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add substance.  
- Broad, relevant skill mix across strategy, platforms, analytics, governance, and multimedia, well aligned to public-sector digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition: “digital communications,” “workflows,” “governance,” and similar phrases recur across sections; tighten to make achievements stand out more distinctly.  
- Improve structure and prioritization: the footer “Recent Projects” is valuable but feels buried; move selected projects higher or integrate them into experience. Also consider consolidating “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.”  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “Ranked among the top public universities...” is unnecessary filler; maintain consistent punctuation and formatting for bullets, date style (“Oct.”/“Sept.”), and capitalization (e.g., “AI-enabled” usage is consistent—good).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad phrases like “building the platforms” with sharper outcome-oriented language tied to enterprise scale.
- Add 1–2 specifics already proven elsewhere in the CV (for example, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) to increase impact.
- Streamline the second sentence to emphasize leadership scope rather than listing capabilities.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector communications platforms, governance, and content operations at enterprise scale. Leads web transformation, analytics ecosystems, editorial workflows, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views and 50+ internal publishers.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The capability list repeats content already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel less repetitive and more executive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, leadership-oriented wording: “Enterprise web modernization,” “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, reporting, and decision-support infrastructure.”
- Group related items to reduce list fatigue and improve flow; suggested version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions like “operations” vs. “experiences”; keep all items noun-based and parallel.
- Consider changing “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to “AI-enabled search and content discovery,” which is more specific and less promotional.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled search” repeat language already used in the header.
- Multimedia/livestream and advocacy communications also recur in Topline Skills and recent project descriptions.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats accomplishments already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more additive and polished.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, outcome-oriented verbs and specify impact where possible: e.g., “improving policy-content discovery,” “supporting ongoing campaign expansion,” or audience/event scale.
- Standardize style and punctuation: use sentence case consistently, hyphenate “bill-level,” and spell out “10-by-20-foot” for cleaner CV style.
- Consider this tighter wording: “Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and a modular architecture designed to scale with the campaign.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and the advocacy video series substantially overlap with current NACo roles in Work Experience.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; consider emphasizing similarly unique projects here.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten around strategic outcomes and distinguish it clearly from the prior NACo staff roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + level: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-oriented bullets; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line about improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/campaigns launched, users supported, toolkits produced, workflow improvements, search/discovery gains, or reduced publishing/support burden.
- Use sharper verbs and reduce detail already covered elsewhere: “Built Drupal campaign microsites and modular storytelling/toolkit components; led AI-enabled search strategy spanning retrieval design, structured content, and user discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal platform,” “governance,” “analytics,” and “organization-wide communications” substantially repeat the 2022–2024 NACo role.
- The microsite and AI search bullets overlap with Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and distinguish strategic ownership here from execution-heavy achievements in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and multi-channel communications for a national membership organization.”
- Combine the website bullets and keep the strongest metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add outcome language where possible: for analytics/governance, specify reporting speed, decision-making improvements, publishing consistency, or reduced bottlenecks.
- Tighten channel language: replace “reaching tens of thousands” / “serving thousands” with exact subscriber/follower counts if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with older video-production bullets; keep this framed as scaling in-house capability, not producing recurring content.
- Governance/editorial coordination overlaps with the consultant and associate director roles; emphasize enterprise leadership here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to this level: emphasize operational ownership, channel growth, and systems/process improvements rather than broad leadership language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to be narrower and more concrete: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets and start with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and measurable if possible: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel distributed across web, email and social.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with ownership: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving consistency and turnaround time.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is too close to the Director role’s channel oversight; use “managed” or “ran” instead.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and the most current differentiators from recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and cross-functional content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and campaign storytelling
- Consider dropping “Public-sector” or “audience-focused” if space is tight; both are implied elsewhere.
- If you want more impact, swap one item for a measurable qualifier, e.g., “Enterprise digital strategy for 10,000+ page, 3.5M annual-view web ecosystems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also repeats multiple work-experience bullets; keep only if phrased more specifically.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms most tied to recent impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a long list to a sharper, senior-level grouping: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are important for target roles; they are lower-signal than your recent Drupal modernization and AI-search work.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based content systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, use “CMS modernization and technical execution” as the lead phrase to connect tools to outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep topline skills strategic and leave full platform inventory to that section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating it verbatim in both places if space is tight.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. This topline item should emphasize strategic analytics capability and decision-making impact, not repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to outcome-oriented capability statement, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy and reporting: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity
- KPI framework design and executive dashboarding
- Web performance, SEO and user behavior analysis
- Put the strategic skills first; tools second.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: “analytics infrastructure for enterprise web modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid listing the exact same tools here and in Technical + IT unless this section is rewritten to stress strategic application.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational leadership and production scope rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more senior and outcome-oriented, e.g. **Multimedia Production & Live Event Operations**
- Replace the current list with:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event operations  
- In-house studio buildout and studio operations  
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows  
- Virtual event delivery for advocacy and member communications
- If space allows, swap one generic item for a scale cue tied to recent work, e.g. “recurring advocacy video programming” or “in-house broadcast studio operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” / “livestream operations” duplicates Core Competencies; use this section to add nuance, not repeat.
- Tool-level detail is already covered in Technical + IT, so avoid listing editing software here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is central to the most recent roles, give it more prominence and trim lower-signal items.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” → put Drupal first and consider signaling depth: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier instead of just names, e.g. “CMS administration, migration and front-end implementation across Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages and GitHub Pages.”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it feels less aligned with the senior enterprise/public-sector positioning.
- Keep this item platform-focused only; save implementation details for the coding/tools line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” especially Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless you consolidate the two sections.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Tag management • Edge/serverless scripting • CI/CD automation
- Replace “HTML5 • CSS3” with “HTML/CSS” for concision; keep “JavaScript” and move “jQuery” to the end or remove if not actively relevant.
- Clarify tools by function: “Google Tag Manager (tracking implementation), Cloudflare Workers (edge scripting), GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation).”
- If space allows, add scope instead of more tools, e.g., “for Drupal-based public websites, analytics instrumentation, and campaign microsites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and “Workflow automation” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Data, Analytics & Optimization unless implementation is the emphasis.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and signal level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and keep only strongest, most relevant tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Remove lower-value/general tools unless they were central in recent roles: Basecamp, Trello, possibly Slack/Teams if space is tight.
- If accurate, add light proficiency framing: “Built workflows in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier; managed delivery in Jira and Asana.”
- Consider renaming to “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools” for clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating them elsewhere with no added specificity.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; listing both may dilute stronger technical signals.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it reads as a generic tool list. Strengthen it by signaling enterprise email/marketing automation capability and aligning wording with the more senior, recent NACo work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (newsletter operations, audience engagement, and campaign delivery)**
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier instead of more tools: **enterprise email communications**, **marketing automation**, or **member communications**
- Keep it concise; this section should support the work experience, not repeat channel ownership already proven there

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email” is already emphasized in multiple NACo roles, so avoid adding descriptive phrases like “managed newsletters” here unless tied to platform capability
- Higher Logic and Mailchimp are older/secondary compared with Dynamics 365; list the most recent/strategic platform first, as you already do

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show level of capability. Since this is a supporting skills item, keep it tighter and more execution-focused than the higher-level skills section.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Tighten and group for readability: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • dashboard development**
- Use more specific phrasing than “Dashboarding”; **dashboard development** or **reporting dashboards** reads stronger.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie these tools to outcomes in recent roles rather than here (e.g., analytics infrastructure, leadership reporting, optimization decisions).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping tools here and moving broader capabilities there.
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” are methods, not tools; if you want cleaner taxonomy, move them to competencies and keep this line platform-focused.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer outcomes if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital communications team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete contributions and scale: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, for member-facing communications.” If possible, add metrics (event/view counts, audience size, publishing volume, turnaround time).
- Tighten management language: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” only if this was informal supervision; otherwise avoid overstating leadership.
- Keep this entry shorter than 2018–2024 roles and position it as the foundation for later leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the launch/early production phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; use more specific execution details here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy/member engagement.
- Consider dropping “organizational” and “contributed to” in favor of stronger verbs like “produced,” “launched,” or “managed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content production; later roles already cover web, video, and multimedia leadership more strongly.
- The “first podcast” is the best non-duplicative detail—keep that prominent.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. In a senior CV, this section should emphasize tools only and keep workflow/production capabilities in the experience or topline skills sections.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to focus on software, not functions: **Creative & Audio/Video Tools**
